text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Democratic Front (UDF) district governor Charles Namijingo has vowed to take his party to court for claiming that he misappropriated party funds while in office.
- Buildings constructed in townships without the permission of town planning committees could be demolished after a civic education campaign by the physical planning and surveys ministry.
- The International Monetary Fund said in a December report that the Structural Adjustment Programme was working well for Malawi after its launch in 1994.

- Traditional Chief Bvumbwe Thyolo on Tuesday accused minister of state, Joseph Kubwalo, of harassing and interrogating him about the defunct Malawi Young Pioneers (MYP), a para-military wing of the former ruling Malawi Congress Party.
- Thirteen people have been charged in a Lilongwe magistrate's court for possession of 118 bags of marijuana.
- The electoral commission has not commented on a public admission by President Bakili Muluzi that he offered fertiliser and cash to an opposition party candidate in a November by-election.
